item.title: Re: Electricity
item.content:encoded:
After electricity suddenly came into existence

Are you talking about actual electricity? Because it has always existed. The ancient Greeks were the first to find out about it as they found out about static electricity.

It would only be in the 1700s with Franklin, Tesla, Faraday, Volta and all the big names will subsequently discover more and more about this force (Voltaic batteries, electrical current and etc..)

The idea that the core of modern civilization is an anomaly that shouldn't exist.

Why is that? I mean yeah we found out about this supposed "anomaly" and then created things out of it. But then it's not abnormal if everyone uses it? But I understand what you're saying. At th end through, it does not really matter. I guess a tiny shift in paradigm but otherwise not much else. Perharps try making it a source of energy that does not exist?

item.title: A Faucet with its Drop.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article (with ACS)

Genre(Optional):Unsure

Page Layout(Optional): Standard, along with certain features including an O5-only document secured with an SCiPNet Login.

Elevator Pitch:

SCP-XXXX has an appearance similar to that of a standard faucet from a manufacturer named "Delta Faucets", with the same look as faucets seen at all homes. SCP-XXXX can function similarly to a usual faucet, for the exception that the water discharged of by SCP-XXXX has a constant discharge rate of 61.6 μL/s, whether supplied with water or not. If so that SCP-XXXX is not supplied with water, the drops discharged of will be more purplish per 17 minutes of use. SCP-XXXX is sentient, and was confirmed of after SCP-XXXX was heard communicating via. Morse Code. This was discovered after a level 4 researcher, who was fluent in Morse, noticed that the drops discharged of by SCP-XXXX took in the order of
…. .. / .- (- -.) (.-) (..) (-.) (- -..- -) / -.. .-. .-.-.-, to which translate to "hi again, dr.".
note: parenthesis on the code due to the preview showing the dashes as a long singular line. also added space to the dashes

A notable anomalous trait is the fact that SCP-XXXX is able to produce melodies with its drops, the range of musical notes that SCP-XXXX can produce ranges from C1 - F7, the range of the human voice. How the drops are able to sound perfectly as these notes are unknown. An incident occurred from this ability, to where in which SCP-XXXX proceeded to play SCP-407 when a Class-D requested for music. Mysteriously however, SCP-XXXX was able to recreate the texture of the song, to which the Class-D reported that SCP-XXXX produced more "drop sounds" despite having only a single drop falling down from the faucet. This was concluded as such to recreate SCP-407's acapella-esque sound.

Another notable trait is the fact that SCP-XXXX's communication is not limited to Morse Code, but also a more complex form of it.

As much so that the waveform of the human voice is made of multiple sine waves combined into one waveform, SCP-XXXX takes this into consideration via translating those wave's hz into singular drops (For example, if it was trying to recreate a 345hz wave, it would discharge 345 drops per second).

A simpler description of this would be the fact that SCP-XXXX breaks down the normal waveform of the human voice when inputted unto an oscillator, and separates it into the waves that were combined to make the waveform in itself. The waveform is made of certain waves ranging from 50hz to 700hz, to which all are 5 minutes length. These pitches from waves made by SCP-XXXX, when combined together, makes a waveform that someone would identify as a recording of someone's voice translated into a wave via. an oscillator. When played, it would make a 5-minute long recording of a human, seemingly in his 40's, talking to someone he calls "Aleph". When questioned of who "Aleph" is, SCP-XXXX replied in Morse Code that "Aleph" was actually the level 4 researcher. Said researcher was notified of this recording, and proceeded to interview SCP-XXXX for further questioning.

Due to this however, SCP-XXXX has tried bringing out information kept secret by the O5, and how it knew those information is currently unknown.

Central Narrative:
The article has interviews with SCP-XXXX, and is in Morse Code, and a visualized explanation of the exceedingly complex other form of communication used by SCP-XXXX. Will be in ACS, classified safe,
disruption class Vlam (due to the SCP-407 incident), Risk class Critical (again because of SCP-407).
The clearance level is unsure of however, as such that it brings out O5 information, but usually dislikes talking about O5-only information. An O5-only interview is present in the article however, so most likely locked off in-universe.

Hook/Attention Grabber:
As much as it is sentient, SCP-XXXX shows a fair degree of omniscience. Morse code known by SCP-XXXX is international, but also fluent in American Morse. The extremely complex communication is basically:

  • Get some waves
  • Translate it to drops
  • Record the hz
  • Get those waves and combine them
  • Get an oscillator and combine them
  • Play the combined wave

In one scenario, SCP-XXXX was actually discovered to be a middle-aged man.

…

Even SCP-XXXX has no recollection on how it got O5 information.

Additional Notes:
He is just a simple man, had a simple life, now he's a faucet. I actually got this idea while in the shower. I stood just in front of the faucet, and was mesmerized by how the drops falling resembled music. Of course it wasn't perfect, nor anomalous. It gave me an idea however. As much as I took 12 hours to get as many ideas as possible, for some reason I was fond of this one even more than one other idea: "A camera that can look at anything, everywhere, without anomalous effect from the viewed object", but of course, that's too boring.

I hope this idea can take off, and please do inform me on any and all mistakes, missed opportunities, or very useful integrations for this thing. Thanks!

Also, SCP-XXXX isn't that powerful, just omniscient. He does regret the SCP-407 incident however.

item.title: Re: The Midas Brick
item.content:encoded:
I do not know how to put it, but the idea is simply…underwhelming?

We are talking about SCP's here, things that could threaten the existence of mankind or the existence of dimensions. And you suggest a brick that could turn things in gold?

First of all, it would create hyperinflation and gold would be worthless. Also many metals are a lot more durable than gold like titanium.

Try integrating a twist to the Curse of Midas to make it more stimulating and interesting. It would require a lot of thinking and effort, but if you put your head to it, it will be worth it!

item.title: Re: Reluctant Wendigo
item.content:encoded:
Got a PM about this, took a look. I'll be honest, I personally don't see this doing well on the mainsite because it relies on a lot of extremely common tropes. I was admittedly skeptical when I read that the hook was meant to be:

A young man is forced to become an anomaly he has no control over. His body's defense mechanisms are hijacked, he cant die, only sent into a feral ravenous, starving state that spurs him to kill, to satiate.

since the "forced to gain abilities" portion is pretty reminiscent of plenty of popular media characters (several trope examples can be found on this page: https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheCorruption) and the guy being a pretty generic murder machine because some shadowy group made them into that is also a very commonly seen setup (the first comparison I thought of was Nemesis from the Resident Evil movies).

I myself wouldn't be interested in reading a full draft of this unless there was some extremely unpredictable/novel material here. The laundry list of abilities and location that churns out anomalous humanoids because "that's just what they do" are both narrative elements that tend to be associated with low-rated articles that don't make the cut. It doesn't matter how weird or specific the monster powers are, the guy's still a generic monster made by a generic monster maker. The fact that you've got a character named after your username that features prominently in the backstory makes me as a reader further skeptical; the audience might get the impression that the story exists solely to set up your character rather than to entertain the readers.

I feel like if you plan on doing more worldbuilding of the sanitarium, you're better off starting with a tale rather than a humanoid SCP article (which get increasingly more and more difficult to write successfully, given how many humanoid articles we already have on the site and how many humanoids/monsters are deleted in a given week). To me it seems like the sanitarium is more likely to lead to unique material than your humanoid here; I recommend that you focus on the former.

item.title: Re: Death is scared, and he wants us.
item.content:encoded:
Came from IRC chat.

I have multiple concerns about this article (as a reader)

+ Critique
- Opened

He came from the sky riding a black horse

Why did death make people want to summon him if he can just summon himself? What is the purpose of such a note. What motivation. Why could no one climb it, which mountain is it?

placed it down on the mountain

What does this mean? He placed it under the mountain? Or he left it there? I am confused.

So she went from fear, to reaction to cold then to hypoxemia? I understand what you are trying to say but the way you formulate it is strange.

For a note that is literally written by Death

This ruins the scary mood you tried to set up.

Below shows an alternate story and some ideas you could use if you are aiming for another rewrite of your SCP. Goodluck!

+ Paramount
- Must fix

Let's break down your SCP:

a note that is literally written by Death that makes people try to summon him, and that could lead to everything getting fucked could be a huge problem

If so, why not just burn it. Why would the SCP want Death to kill everyone. Hence why the need for a numbered SCP. However, you could make it a:

SCP-XXXX is a papyrus that attracts people. Upon reading it, the user will try to summon death. If done successfully, Death will arrive causing thousands in the proximity of the user to die. It cannot be burned, it cannot be destroyed.

Then you could play with this idea and make it that people try to break in? Something like that so that it's importance is more significant. Play with the dangerousness of Death.

item.title: Re: Living on repeat
item.content:encoded:
The idea is that every death will trigger a new set of logs, as every trip through is slightly different. Through this process, you are going to see the effect of living multiple lifetimes in Foundation custody,

At first, you see a man who is surprised to be seen for what he is, though the foundation is still not entirely sure what they've got. He initially chooses to keep returning to the Foundation out of curiosity, though he hints that he takes some "breather lives" in between.

As the novelty wears off and the foundation is better managing his containment, he starts to show signs of listlessness and boredom, slowly coming to terms with containment. He is a little confused to, as he doesn't remember living so many lives so similarly one after the other.

This culminates in a verbal fight with the lead researcher, after which he takes the first opportunity to suicide. The next set of logs show a changed man, one that has willingly followed the same path with major difference: the person he kills before becoming a D-Class is the same person that was the lead researcher.

Upon figuring this out, the foundation brings him in for an interview to ask about it. At this point I want to reference one of the written about XK class end of world scenarios, probably SCP 5000, where he lives a fairly successful life uncontained until the event. This wakes him up to the idea that he needs to live with containment, as the world literally ended when he left containment.

He says he wanted something new, so he came back but ensured a change in management for his wellbeing. At this point the mental mileage is really showing, and his demeanor is more exhausted than aggressive. He's willing to play ball, but wants to know if the foundation wants to be on his team.

It kinda ends on a cliff hanger, as he remains in containment but only just. The foundation still worries that something might happen to cause his death, and are doing what they can to find a way to indefinitely prolong his life to prevent the next loop from coming. The 05's are against using the fountain of life, and the ethics committee is of the opinion that a permanent death would be more ethical than eternal life, so they are looking into other methods to end or contain what they are classifying as a "center of reality" scenario.

item.title: Re: Draft "Disconnected Restroom"
item.content:encoded:
Note, I am not the most well-read or experienced user. Reach out to members of the Butterfly Roster for more informed criticism.

Phrases in quotes are my suggestions.

Line By Line
hiya howdy howya doin

The hallway leading to SCP-XXXX has to be guarded by at least one security personnel at all times.

The hallway is to be guarded. Passive voice. Also, the "at least one" clause is unnecessary. How can a hallway be guarded by less than one guard?

Cleaning staff may flush if they hear noises coming from SCP-XXXX, but must record when they do so.

"Cleaning staff are to flush if they hear noises coming from SCP-XXXX, and must make record of doing so."

At no time should SCP-XXXX be used as originally intended.

Too vague. If we haven't read the article yet, we don't know what the original intent is.
"At no time should SCP-XXXX be used as a waste receptacle."

Side note: add line breaks between paragraphs. Necessary for readability.

The building housing SCP-XXXX has been bought by the Foundation and is used as [REDACTED]. To the outside it is advertised as telemarketing firm. Unauthorized entry should be responded to by calling the local police.

The ConProcs don't generally need detail about the Site cover stories unless it's related to the nature of the anomaly. Also, there are armed guards in this building. Involvement of local police is redundant. "Provisional Site-XXXX has been established in the building housing SCP-XXXX. Unauthorized entry is forbidden."

It consists of two adjacent restrooms, one for males and one for females.

"It consists of two adjacent restrooms with standard male/female designations."

Both areas have two sinks and four stalls

"Both areas possess"

The restrooms are working as normally expected.

"SCP-XXXX functions as expected for a public restroom."

as underground exploration and sub-surface scans showed.

"have shown"

Electricity however is connected as expected.

Commas after "electricity" and "however".

The planning company found that no plans existed where the water supply or sewer access was depicted for the building housing SCP-XXXX.

"Contractors found that water supply and sewer access were absent from all plans of the building."

A check of the canalization confirmed that no access to the building exists and the Foundation was informed.

"A check of the canalization confirmed the absence of water mains and sewer lines. The Foundation was subsequently notified."

The initially deployed MTF ███ secured SCP-XXXX under cover of the reconstruction project which was immediately canceled.

No reason to censor an MTF. "MTF-BLANK initially secured SCP-XXXX under cover of the renovation project. All construction plans were subsequently cancelled."

The employees of the offices in the building were detained and questioned. During the interviews medical and psychological examinations were conducted as well.

"Employees of the offices in the building were detained, questioned, and subjected to medical and psychological examination."

There was no indication of any influence on the persons working in the building.

This is simply untrue, given the information you provide in the next sentence.

Dr. Vitruv noted during the interviews that many employees had rather fond memories of the restrooms, finding relief being there, using the facilities or simply running the water.

"Dr. Vitruv noted that during the interviews, many employees recalled fond memories of the restrooms. Subjects reported feelings of calm or relief when using the facilities or simply running the water."

Sampling the tap water, it was discovered that it matches the composition and requirements of most of the tap water in the United States as shown in document XXXX-2.

"Sampling of the tap water revealed that it meets all composition requirements in the state of ██. It possesses no components that might aid in tracing its origin. For details on the composition of water obtained from SCP-XXXX, see Document-XXXX-2."

For the used water / waste see Post-Experiment report XXXX-4

"For compositional analysis of black- and grey-water obtained from SCP-XXXX, see Post-experiment Report XXXX-4."

Experiment XXXX-1: Audio Transcript

Add a note clarifying that the exploration is taking place via drone.

Frank:

Use Frank's full blacked-out name.

Note: Line breaks should be added throughout this log.

Note2: During this log there are multiple instances of ellipses ("…") that are spaced incorrectly. They should be placed directly after the word they follow with no space in-between.

As per experiment report XXXX-4-B and under strict safety measures four point one litres of [REDACTED] were inserted into the sewer section of SCP-XXXX using the first booth of the men's room. The liquid was flushed using a total of eighty litres of SCP-XXXX tap water. As [REDACTED] is a potent and safe tracer it was believed to enable us to identify the exit of SCP-XXXX. Unfortunately we did not manage to confirm any result.
About two months after the experiment a meteorological satellite under control of the ████ found traces of the used substance in the southern Atlantic. It is currently unknown if this finding correlates to SCP-XXXX.
I am awaiting clearance to repeat the experiment.
Dr. Vitruv

I have multiple issues with this note. Firstly, redacting the tracer liquid adds nothing to the article and makes the note significantly harder to read. Appears as if you simply did not want to research a traceable liquid. Similarly, there is no reason to redact the controller of the satellite. Lastly, there are multiple instances of missing commas. Dr. Vitruv should sign the note with a dash, like this:
"—Dr. Vitruv"

a man calling himself Michael (actual identity unknown, assumed to be a local homeless man)

"a local homeless man calling himself "Michael" (actual identity unconfirmed)"

The hallway guard was absent at that time due to a medical emergency.

This seems like gross incompetence on behalf of whoever is managing containment. Perhaps,

"The hallway guard was momentarily absent during shift turnover."

According to post-incident interrogation Michael had to urgently use the restroom, so he opened the (due to the emergency unlocked) front door and walked into SCP-XXXX.

"According to post-incident interrogation Michael urgently needed to use the restroom, and therefore entered SCP-XXXX through the main door, which was momentarily unlocked due to REASON"

Note: you're going to have to come up with a new reason for the door being unlocked. I can't think of one off the top of my head.

He described hearing a violent grown directly after he flushed - and experiencing a sharp pain in the lower abdomen before loosing consciousness.

"He described hearing a violent groan directly after flushing, and experienced a sharp lower-abdominal pain before losing consciousness."

bleeding from a head wound due to a broken door.

The meaning of this is unclear. How exactly did Michael hurt his head?

Overall thoughts
phew that took a while

While I overall enjoyed this skip, I don't believe it's quite ready for the mainlist in its current state. Specifically, the anomalous effect needs to be fleshed out. It's just… missing a little something.

Now, I very much enjoy how your article creates mystery, so going forward you have a tightrope to walk between showing us interesting and intriguing effects, and maintaining the simplicity of the premise. That's a difficult task, but I believe it can be done.

In conclusion I would say that perhaps 10% more information about the anomaly would add some much-needed intrigue, but 15% would be too much. Act on that as you see fit.

I wish you the best of luck and hope to see this on the mainlist sometime soon.

Have a great day!

item.title: ONE YEAR/REMEMBER DEATH
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The anomaly was a former channel on the media site “YouTube” that was active from 11/15/19 to 11/15/20 exactly one year from its creation.

The channel uploaded what would seem like fun original content but was littered with cognitohazardous material that has now been completely neutralized. Two humanoids are present in every video and host the channel. Both entities are almost identical to two other famous people but are not the same people.

Subjects who view any of the 365 videos are instantly met with a clock that counts down starting from 365:00:00. The anomaly’s effects immediate initiate at the start of every video by infecting and manipulating the subject’s mind making them perceive the two entities as gods and begin to worship the two entities in nonsensical and sometimes violent ways. Afflicted subjects attempt to spread the anomaly through social media and other chat related applications.

The anomaly can not be deleted directly by YouTube since attempts to do so crash all electronic devices.

The two entities seen in every video seem to not be a part of our dimension but from another reality. Since they cannot be located and have been seen with anomalous items that do cannot exist in our reality.
Central Narrative: The Narrative would dictate all of the foundations attempts to neutralize the anomaly and work with YouTube to contain the anomaly from spreading. Millions of viewers have already been infected by the anomaly and spread of the anomaly drastically increases. The Foundation worries that an AK end of the world scenario could occur as tens of millions of people rapidly fall under the anomaly’s influence. As governments collapse and people perform violent rituals in the streets the channel finally reaches its climatic end

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Based on a real experiment conducted on the same website.

Additional Notes: The central narrative would begin by detailing the small amount of infection but slowly starts getting worse and worse until the end. Not all details described here it would be too long.

item.title: Re: Medicine Man - first scp idea
item.content:encoded:
It just feels boring, basic, and not a good fit for the site.

The Bold Statement says my first thought of this SCP, and without further statements, here's the review.

The Review
– hide block

The Pitch
It just feels boring, and outdated. It did not peak my interest what so ever. It didn't make me think, Huh, that's a neat SCP Idea, I just read it and grew more bored of the concept with every sentence. A sculpture is an something that has been used many times of the Wiki, as doing a simple tag search I found 55 SCPs that revolve around a Sculpture as an SCP, So already, that's a problem, you could find another object, any other object, and I would be fine. And for it to revolve around you dropping your guard just feels very "SCP-173" like, it's too similar.
Now the way the Sculpture has its anomalous effect is that you lose attention in the Sculpture, that just sounds very basic, and boring. Now, to where the Medicine Man switches to another sculpture, why not just contain him when he's switching? Don't add shit where he's "Impossible to contain." Cause then that's going to make this entire SCP just feel like a child's piece of literature. Also how the fuck would the SCP Foundation know if a Sculpture has a consciousness? As you make it seem like you make a person an object that can't move, speak, breathe, touch, blink, etc. Well how would anyone know that the Sculpture was conscious?

Central Narrative
Oh boy, this is what pissed me off the most out of your Idea, the fact that you think the Foundation would Attempt to recruit a semi-dangerous SCP who tells people they have lost the ability to concentrate, and could switch a person to an eternal hell of not moving, is a damn ludicrous thought! They would secure this SCP down in a single room, maybe test it a bit, and they would probably never use it again. The SCP site is a prison, not a place of recruitment or a hotel, but a place of exploitation, research, and containment. If an SCP shows any sign of being dangerous, I would think it's safe to assume that they would never want to use it for the good, as any SCP could have undiscovered traits that could cause major harm to the world.

Conclusion
I may have been harsh, and this may be your first SCP Idea, but it just doesn't seem to fit for a modern like SCP, maybe a few years ago the site would let this fly but times have changed.

item.title: Re: My first SCP failed, can anyone give me advice about why?
item.content:encoded:
I'll preface this by saying I'm not an official critter, nor a seasoned author (I've written one SCP that did… okay, but wasn't highly received.)

I think the clinical tone could use some work. Moreover, some of the dialogue feels a little bit clunky at times. Some parts are difficult to read because the article tends to repeat itself a lot. For example, twice you mention mention how the substance will corrode into unglazed ceramic. Additionally, oxytocin/serotonin/dopamine levels are repeatedly mentioned, when instead you could say something like:

Instances of SCP-5245-2 share a similar bodily composition to SCP-5245, complete with
identical hormones and neurotransmitters.

I also feel like there's designation bloat. SCP-5245-1 is a copy of the mask that's mentioned once, then never again. I'd lose that, and simply change SCP-5245-2 to SCP-5245-1. You could say:

When in the proximity of an individual that lacks a face covering, SCP-5245 will
manufacture an identical copy of the mask from its body and forcibly place it upon
the victim (hereby referred to as an instance of SCP-5245-1.)

Overall, I think there's a good idea, but the conclusion left me feeling very underwhelmed. I'd recommend visiting the Idea Critique Forum to see what the critters think (who are much better writers then I'll ever be). Keep corresponding with them until you get greenlights, then write a draft, then go to the Draft Critique Forum. Then, if you've gotten good feedback, post to the main site.

item.title: Re: Time: Limited
item.content:encoded:
The first question I have is what is the SCP? You talk about a series of radio transmissions and then an abnormal mass that’s heading towards earth. Your elevator pitch makes me believe that the SCP is the radio signals, however your hook contradicts this and makes me think it is the abnormal mass.

My bad, clarification should have been added. The main anomaly is the signals, the mass is a secondary anomaly I.E. SCP-XXXX-1.

My second question would be how does an astronomer notices this mass? You clearly state that the signals are originating from a galaxy, implying that the foundation can’t narrow it down any further than that; but then you contradict this by saying an astronomer notices a mass exiting the galaxy. For one, the astronomer would barely be able to see the galaxy through the dust plane in the Milky Way, let alone notice a mass heading towards earth, and the mass would have to be absolutely massive for the scientist to see it. And something that big would collapse in on itself due to its own gravitational pull.

This part of your critique, although understandable and will result in adjustments down the line, I feel is not necessarily that big of a problem. The foundation has access to insane technology, both anomalous and non-anomalous, so it isn't too far fetched to believe that they have the means to spot the mass.

I also don't feel that the astronomer noticing the mass exiting the galaxy contradicts anything to do with the signals? There's a stark contrast to invisible radio signals travelling through space and a massive mass exiting a galaxy. I do see your point, however.

As for the mass collapsing in on itself, it can fairly easily be explained as an anomalous effect (although a cheap explanation, it works).

Nice critique! Some parts felt nit picky but there is a good bit of validity.

Keep in mind that I only have one article and cannot greenlight. Reach out to some more experienced users for more informed critique.

I really like the bare bones of this idea. However, I'm unsure of this line:

Hyper-detailed descriptions of -a -b and -c objects that indicate they are not what they are named to be.

This is worded in such a way that I'm confused as to its meaning. I understand that you might be being intentionally vague so as not to spoil your article, but that kind of defeats the purpose of an attention grabber, no?

I'm also worried about how this would be executed. You say this:

They end up being re-contained three separate times as their process of describing their own containment causes it to change.
